title: Population characteristics — Ongoing characteristics
description: UK Biobank fields in the category Population characteristics > Ongoing characteristics, as selected by the CD3 researchers.

f190.title: Reason lost to follow-up

oneOf.title: Death reported to UK Biobank by a relative
NHS records indicate they are lost to follow-up
NHS records indicate they have left the UK
UK Biobank sources report they have left the UK
Participant has withdrawn consent for future linkage

f190.$comment: Source coding: encoding 1965. If more than one reason applies, only the earliest is recorded. Source notes this field has not been updated since May 2017.

f191.title: Date lost to follow-up
f191.$comment: If more than one reason for loss to follow-up applies, only the date of the earliest is recorded. Date format YYYY-MM-DD (ISO 8601) is assumed, not stated by the source (D015).

f20005.title: Email access

oneOf.title: Unusable, email address failed or withdrawn

f20005.$comment: Source coding: encoding 1007. Deduced from whether the participant supplied an email address to UK Biobank; flagged Unusable on a syntax error, a bounce-back, or a withdrawal request. The address itself is never released to researchers.

f20143.title: Date of last personal contact with UK Biobank
f20143.$comment: Most recent occasion a participant personally contributed data: an assessment centre visit, an online questionnaire, or returning a device. Date format YYYY-MM-DD (ISO 8601) is assumed, not stated by the source (D015).

f20144.title: Mode of last personal contact with UK Biobank

f20145.title: Number of personal contacts with UK Biobank
f20145.$comment: Count of occasions a participant personally contributed data (assessment centre visit, online questionnaire, or device use/return). No plausibility bound stated (D013).

f110007.title: Newsletter communications, date sent
f110007.$comment: Dispatch date only; does not imply successful receipt or that the recipient read the newsletter. Date format YYYY-MM-DD (ISO 8601) is assumed, not stated by the source (D015).
